dod_intent_evidence: Air Force 2022 SBIR Phase II ($1,249,907) for a C2 tent-wall projection system explicitly framed around warfighter/A2AD/SWaP needs, plus a 2024 Phase II SBIR for Space Domain Operations and Training dome visualization (8 total Phase I/II awards, $5.2M since 2017) — see SBIR/STTR record and News sections.
score_evidence: 'STL software aggregated content from 4 Projectors, 9.6K resolution, 53 million pixels per frame at 30 frames per second, 1.4 billion pixels per second' → lab_language_intensity (spec-brag framing, though for a commercial museum install, not defense)

'Battlefield display technology has not evolved beyond 2D commercially available systems that do not meet the stringent SWaP requirements for Agile Combat Employment required to survive A2AD environments...providing the warfighter what they NEED at a SWaP they can AFFORD' → deployment_awareness_absence scored LOW (they are unusually fluent in SWaP-C/A2AD language — a 'they get it, still a keep, bottom of list' case per calibration rule) and operator_absence scored LOW (explicit, repeated 'warfighter' and 'deployed unit' framing)

Firmographic note: 'Summit Technology Laboratory employs 5 people (-33.3% YoY, -3 [people])' → stage_pressure (shrinking tiny team carrying an active 2022 AF Phase II and fresh 2024 Phase II simultaneously)

blind_spots.blind_spot: System is built on 'lightweight consumer grade projectors' meshed together rather than ruggedized hardware
blind_spots.operator_reality: Consumer-grade optics and electronics degrade fast under field dust, heat, humidity, and transport vibration — the SBIR abstract talks fluently about SWaP-C requirements but the actual hardware choice trades ruggedization for cost/weight in a way that will surface as field failures
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Company's core commercial product (museum/simulator installs) is built around off-the-shelf AV gear in climate-controlled venues, and that engineering default carried into the defense pitch
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Leveraging our industry leading expertise and experience to mesh multiple lightweight consumer grade projectors into a 4-8K HD interactive immersive projection

blind_spots.blind_spot: 'Automated recalibration runs' depend on a continuously working camera-plus-compute pipeline
blind_spots.operator_reality: No mention anywhere of what happens when the calibration camera lens fogs, dusts over, or the compute unit loses power in the field — the product's core value prop ('push the button and get it done') assumes the sensing loop always works, which is exactly the DDIL-adjacent failure mode that breaks automated systems in the field
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Calibration automation was engineered and proven in indoor commercial venues (Discovery Cube, MoPop) where power and climate are guaranteed
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Allows scheduled or automated recalibration runs in minutes. No more waiting for hours or days for the technician to arrive. Just push the button and get it done.

blind_spots.blind_spot: A C2 tent-wall display projecting 'a deployed unit's data needs' has no ATO/RMF/CMMC/data-handling language anywhere in the pack
blind_spots.operator_reality: A system rendering command-and-control data onto the physical walls of a tactical operations center is by definition handling sensitive/classified information, yet there is zero mention of an authorization pathway for that data or the projection system's compute stack
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Team's expertise (Aditi Majumder et al.) is computer vision/graphics research, not government compliance; the SBIR abstract stays entirely in the technical-feasibility lane
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Imagine a deployed unit projecting all of its data needs directly onto the sides of the command/C2 tent creating a massive surround presentation while maintaining the highest quality resolution and projected form

opener_hook: STL's 2022 Air Force Phase II SBIR proved 4-8K projection on a moving tent wall for C2 displays, with a second Phase II now running on Space Domain Operations dome visualization — is there an ATO path yet for the data those tent-wall displays will show?
what_they_do: Computer-vision projection-mapping SaaS (Artemis) that auto-calibrates multi-projector immersive displays, sold to museums/simulators commercially and adapted via SBIR into deformable-surface C2 tent-wall and space-domain-awareness displays for the Air Force.
